shifts.summary: Most candidates reported the paper as moderate overall. Reasoning was generally easy but some found it tough due to time pressure. General Awareness was mainly static with a few current affairs and heavily based on previous year questions. Quantitative aptitude was the most challenging section with many lengthy calculations, while English was considered easy and largely PYQ based.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Most questions were doable but time pressure caused skips. Many statement‑type and coding‑decoding items appeared. Logic was easy for most, with few dice questions.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GA was mainly static with a few current affairs items. Questions were heavily based on previous year papers. Topics covered history, business, and key constitutional facts.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant contained many advanced calculations and lengthy items. Time management was a major issue, with several candidates skipping questions that took more than 30 seconds. Topics ranged from geometry to profit‑loss and compound interest.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was easy and largely based on previous year questions. Candidates performed well on passage comprehension and grammar, though some found active‑passive items challenging.

shifts.summary: Candidates found the shift overall easy to moderate. Reasoning was generally easy but some found it moderate due to timing pressure. Quantitative aptitude showed mixed difficulty with most reporting moderate. English was mostly easy with good attempts across the board.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: A few questions were left because of the sectional timer, most questions were doable, and a small number of new pattern items caused slight timing issues. Some items were time‑consuming but not hard.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GA segment was completed quickly with 25 questions in 8 minutes, and the content was largely traditional GK and criminal law topics.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Two long Time‑Work questions ate time, arithmetic calculations were lengthy, and while some advanced parts were easy once formulas were known, overall timing was critical.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Grammar and comprehension were easy, though many words made full attempts harder; candidates made 5‑6 guesses and took a bit more time on the passage.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 10 October 2026 was analysed across two reported shifts and one pending shift. Candidates described Shift 1 as moderate overall, while Shift 2 was perceived as easy to moderate, with some variation in responses. The reported good‑attempt ranges are 75–90 for Shift 1 and 71–94 for Shift 2, but these figures are unofficial and SSC normally normalises scores across all shifts. Analysis for Shift 3 will be added after the shift concludes and sufficient candidate feedback is collected.

faqs.q: What overall difficulty level was reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was described as moderate overall, whereas Shift 2 was reported as easy to moderate, with some candidates noting timing pressure. Shift 3 has not yet been analysed, so its difficulty rating will be posted later.

faqs.q: How many candidates attempted the sections successfully on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: For Shift 1, the good‑attempt range was 75–90 overall, and for Shift 2 it was 71–94 overall. These numbers are based on candidate feedback and are not official SSC statistics.

faqs.q: Which sections were considered most challenging on 10 October 2026?
faqs.a: Quantitative Aptitude was reported as the most challenging section in both Shift 1 and Shift 2, with lengthy calculations causing difficulty. Reasoning was generally easy but some candidates found it moderate due to time pressure, while English was largely easy and based on previous‑year questions.

faqs.q: When will the analysis for Shift 3 of the 10 October 2026 exam be available?
faqs.a: The analysis for Shift 3 will be added a few hours after the shift ends, once enough candidate reviews have been collected.

faqs.q: Are the figures presented for the 10 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 exam official?
